text:
Zach Hyman's season has been interrupted twice. He hurt himself in the preseason finale, played the opener, then missed six games; he came back, got hit into the boards against Detroit on Oct. 26 and missed five more with a neck injury. Back since Nov. 7, he has scored 3 goals in his last three games, including the winner against Philadelphia on Nov. 15.

At 34, he still lives at the net. His 4 goals sit on 3.76 expected goals, a measure of the quality of his chances, so the finishing is honest. The volume is lower than last year, when he scored 31 goals in 58 games. His chance rate is down to 1.16 expected goals per 60 from 1.82, and he is playing on the second line rather than beside Connor McDavid.

Evolving-Hockey rated him a real play driver last season, 98th percentile among forwards in how much offense his team created with him on the ice, while noting his teammates were among the league's best. He has also credited coach Mike Babcock, in a Yahoo Sports headline, with bringing "new life to locker room." The question is health more than talent.
headline: Hyman keeps getting hurt, and keeps finding the net
